```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

These 2.10.3 examples follow the frozen recipe-language-2 contract and stay
unevaluated until compiler integration. Patient tables are assigned beside the
data; use reviewed DataSHIELD methods to analyse them. The previous chapter
explains populations and index dates.

## Choose rows, then columns

The simple layer is enough for baseline values around an index. Define concept
sets for your vocabulary; the following IDs illustrate a diabetes study.

```{r}
library(dsOMOPClient)
index <- omop_event("condition_occurrence", 201826, descendants = TRUE)
study <- omop_study(
  index = index, require = list(age = c(18, NA)),
  baseline = list(age = omop_age(), sex = omop_sex(),
    hba1c = omop_value_at_index("measurement", 3004410,
                               tolerance = c(-90, 30), unit = 8554),
    visits = omop_count("visit_occurrence", before = 365)),
  outputs = "baseline")
recipe_to_code(study)
```

`before = 365` includes days -365 through 0; `after = 30` includes days 1
through 30. Choose only one of `before`, `after` and `window`. Without one,
shortcuts use all history through index day. A numeric unit restricts rows to
that unit; it does not convert values. `omop_unit()` supplies explicit affine
conversions, applied before predicates and reducers.

## Education level and cause of death in one wide table

An education question is the observation's `observation_concept_id`; the
answer (primary, secondary, and so on) is `value_as_concept_id`. Choose the
question's concept ID from the site's vocabulary. `education_question` below
is that study input, not a universal education code.

The familiar table/format spelling remains available:

```{r}
education <- omop_variable(
  name = "education", table = "observation", concept_id = education_question,
  value_source = "value_as_concept_id", type = "categorical", format = "last_value")
cause <- omop_variable(name = "cause_of_death", table = "death",
  column = "cause_concept_id", type = "categorical", format = "first_value")
```

The 2.10.3 advanced spelling names an event and reducer. This selects the last
coded answer through the index day, avoiding post-index education updates:

```{r}
education_event <- omop_event("observation", concepts = education_question)
education <- omop_variable(name = "education", event = education_event,
  type = "categorical",
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id",
                         window = omop_window(NULL, 0), missing = "skip"))
cause <- omop_variable(name = "cause_of_death", event = omop_event("death"),
  type = "categorical",
  reducer = omop_reduce("first_value", value = "cause_concept_id"))
pop <- omop_population(id = "patients", index = omop_index(index))
recipe <- omop_recipe(
  populations = list(patients = pop),
  variables = list(education = education, cause_of_death = cause),
  outputs = list(profile = omop_output("profile", format = "wide",
    rows = "patients", grain = "episode",
    columns = c("education", "cause_of_death"))),
  options = list(translate_concepts = TRUE))
recipe_explain(recipe, conns = conns)
result <- recipe_execute(recipe, out = c(profile = "D_profile"), conns = conns)
```

Translation follows the declared concept type, including renamed wide columns;
it must not depend on an `_concept_id` suffix. This is a 2.10.3 integration
requirement: verify translated names and retained IDs on your integrated build.
`cause_of_death` is the coded cause, not proof that everyone has died; missing
cause stays NA. It is an outcome description and may use future information,
so do not treat it as a pre-index predictor.

For a dataset that stores answers as text, this spelling illustrates the
requested alternative, but it is deliberately refused under ordinary policy:

```{r}
education_text <- omop_variable(name = "education_text", table = "observation",
  concept_id = education_question, value_source = "value_as_string",
  type = "categorical", format = "last_value")
# recipe_to_plan() refuses a recipe that releases this class-1 source.
```

`value_as_string` and `cause_source_value` are free source text (class 1).
Selecting a categorical type or renaming the column does not make them safe.
Use coded `value_as_concept_id` and `cause_concept_id` for the portable recipe.
An administrator's existing sensitive-column override is not permission to
use text predicates or to alias protected source columns through mutation.

## Understand the reducer

A reducer summarizes an event stream per person or episode. Count and binary
return zero for an available empty stream. Value reducers return NA; a sum
returns zero. Unavailable sources and undefined required anchors yield NA,
including for counts. `first_value` and `last_value` select one complete row
by date and deterministic source key; `missing = "skip"` skips missing values
before selection, whereas `keep` retains the selected row's missing value.
Selected value, unit, operator and date must refer to the same row.

```{r}
rx <- omop_event("drug_exposure", 1503297, descendants = TRUE)
era <- omop_era(rx, gap = 30, persistence = 0)
covered <- omop_variable(event = era,
  reducer = omop_reduce("covered_days", window = omop_window(1, 365),
                         observed_only = TRUE))
observed <- omop_observed_days(omop_window(1, 365))
```

Course duration includes grace and persistence; `covered_days` unions recorded
coverage and excludes those gaps. With `observed_only = TRUE`, the numerator
and `observed_days` denominator use the same observed days. Thus PDC can be
computed as covered/observed, with a zero denominator becoming NA. MPR uses
`supply_days`, not `duration_sum`; overlapping supplies have different meanings
in those measures. Stockpiling exposes a separate `effective_supply` relation
that must be selected explicitly. Native comorbidity scores use conditions
through their reference date (the episode index by default); a consumer with
no unique index needs a fixed date.

## Choose an output shape

| Shape | Intended use |
|---|---|
| `wide` | One row per declared person or episode; selected variables become columns. |
| `long` | Event rows from `sources`; a reducer needs `broadcast = TRUE` to repeat over them. |
| `survival` | Named TAR components; first event, competing risk, recurrent events, counting process or multi-state as declared. |
| `intervals` | Recorded or constructed intervals. |
| `person_period` | Dense or sparse panels with explicit bins and source identities. |
| `temporal_covariates`, `sparse` | Covariate rows plus reference companions. |
| `membership`, `dictionary` | Patient membership, or plan/vocabulary reference metadata respectively. |
| `joined` | A declared, validated composition of private inputs. |

An indexed population requires episode grain unless a person-grain output
explicitly collapses episodes (`first_episode`, `last_episode` or `any`).
A dense available-but-event-free source keeps its declared columns and zero/NA
rules; an unavailable source is NA. Multi-concept source columns retain concept
identity. Carry-forward is per source and concept, evaluated at period start.

Survival windows and censoring are explicit. Native v2 adds no implicit
cohort-end cap; request `index_end` when intended. A named TAR yields its own
inventory entry, such as `D_tte.itt`. Each independently accessible patient
component must pass distinct-person support; a passing roster does not permit
a small event component to escape. Reference companions are released only
with their passing family.

## Publish and analyse

```{r}
recipe <- recipe_set_publish(recipe, "profile")
result <- recipe_execute(recipe, out = c(profile = "D_profile"),
                         output_mode = "memory", conns = conns)
# Use the symbols in result's committed inventory for downstream analysis.
dsBaseClient::ds.dim("D_profile", datasources = conns)

# Assigned ordinary analysis columns can be transformed server-side.
ds.omop.mutate("D_profile", has_cause = !is.na(cause_of_death),
                newobj = "D_profile_derived", conns = conns)
ds.omop.filter("D_profile_derived", expr = omop_where(has_cause == TRUE),
                newobj = "D_deaths", conns = conns)
```

Fresh names may differ when destinations already exist. Verbs publish a new
patient object and recheck its own support; mutations cannot read or write
person, episode or set keys. They use a closed expression language, not
arbitrary R. In-place mutation (`newobj = x`) keeps a rollback copy until
federation commit is verified and invalidates DP provenance.

Staged mode writes private server-local Parquet (CSV fallback) and returns
validated descriptors, not download URLs. A server-side consumer resolves a
committed component with `omopStagedDatasetPath()`. Uncommitted or revoked
components are unreadable. Keep the returned dynamic inventory rather than
predicting component suffixes.

Exact birth components and exact age may be assigned on request. Assigned
age bands accept any increasing integer grid starting at zero, including
`c(0, 18, 19, 65)`, without per-band suppression. Aggregate endpoints retain
their existing admission, banding and suppression rules; a permitted assigned
column does not grant an unrestricted aggregate release.
